September 25, 1976) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is the suspended head coach of the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). After playing [[college basketball]] with the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]], he was selected third overall in the [[1997 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]]. A [[point guard]], Billups played for seven NBA franchises over spent his 17-year basketball career, most notably the [[Detroit Pistons]], for whom he won the [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player|NBA Finals MVP]] in 2004 after helping the Pistons beat the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the [[2004 NBA Finals|Finals]].{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/steve_aschburner/11/03/billups/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102042932/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/steve_aschburner/11/03/billups/|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 2, 2012|title=Back home after trade, Billups has something to prove with Nuggets|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=November 3, 2008|first=Steve|last=Aschburner}} He was given the nickname "'''Mr. Big Shot'''" for making late-game shots with Detroit.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/eticket/story?page=090511/billups&redirected=true|title=The Disposable Superstar|publisher=ESPN.com|work=[[Outside the Lines]]|date=May 11, 2009|first=Tom|last=Friend}}{{cite web |last=Bailey |first=Andy |title=Ranking the Top 50 NBA Playoff Performers of All Time |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10124068-ranking-the-top-50-nba-playoff-performers-of-all-time |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=June 22, 2024 |date=June 18, 2024 }} A five-time [[NBA All-Star]], a three-time [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA]] selection, and two-time [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive]] selection, Billups also played for the [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], [[New York Knicks]], and [[Los Angeles Clippers]] during his NBA career. He was inducted into the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]] in 2024.{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/news/hall-of-fame-class-of-2024 |title=Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame announces 13 inductees for Class of 2024 |date=April 6, 2024 |website=NBA.com |access-date=April 6, 2024}} Billups worked as a studio analyst after his retiring from playing in 2014. The Pistons [[retired number|retired]] his No. 1 jersey in 2016.{{Cite web|title = Billups: 'I just wanted to be a champion'|url = http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2016/02/10/jersey-retirement-emotional-experience-billups/80208150/|website = Detroit News|access-date = February 19, 2016}} He started coaching as an assistant for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] during the 2020–21 season. Billups was appointed as head coach of the Trail Blazers in 2021. In October 2025, Billups was arrested by the [[FBI]] for his alleged involvement in [[2025 NBA illegal gambling prosecution|an illegal gambling scheme]]. He was subsequently suspended indefinitely by the NBA, with [[Tiago Splitter]] serving as acting head coach until he was hired to be head coach of the [[2026–27 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]] following the season.

'''Charles Oakley''' (born December 18, 1963) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Oakley is best known for playing ten of his nineteen seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] with the [[New York Knicks]]. As a [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]], he consistently ranked as one of the best rebounders and defensive players in the NBA. He also played for the [[Chicago Bulls]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Washington Wizards]], and [[Houston Rockets]]. From 2017-2025, he was the coach of the [[Killer 3's]] of the [[BIG3]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://big3.com/players/charles-oakley/|title=Charles Oakley|publisher=[[BIG3]]|access-date=April 9, 2020}}{{deadlink|date=January 2026}}</ref>

During his nine full seasons with the Knicks, he was a member of the team that made the [[1999 NBA Finals]]. Ward was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] during the [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04 season]] and spent his final year in 2005 with the [[Houston Rockets]]. Following his retirement as a player, Ward began a coaching career and has served as the head coach of the Rattlers since 2025. He was inducted to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2006.

'''Christopher Claus Andersen''' (born July 7, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Nicknamed "'''Birdman'''" for his wingspan and blocking prowess,<ref>{{cite web |title=Chris Andersen NBA Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/anderch01.html |access-date=March 7, 2013 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> Andersen was born in [[Long Beach, California]], grew up in [[Iola, Texas]], and played one year at [[Blinn College]].<ref name=biopage>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/chris_andersen/bio.html |title=NBA.com: Chris Andersen Bio Page |work=NBA.com |access-date=July 10, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130621034019/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/chris_andersen/bio.html |archive-date=June 21, 2013 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> Andersen began his professional career in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] and the American minor leagues.

After getting called up to play in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) from the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]], Andersen would go on to play for the [[Denver Nuggets]] and [[New Orleans Hornets]]. He received a [[list of people banned or suspended by the NBA|two-year ban from the NBA]] in [[2005–06 NBA season|2006]] for violating the league's drug policy,<ref name="comeback">{{cite web |date=January 27, 2006 |others=The Associated Press |title=Hornets' Andersen kicked out of NBA for drug use |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2308918 |access-date=June 10, 2013 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> but was reinstated on March 4, 2008, and re-signed with the Hornets the next day. He returned to Denver later in 2008, and remained with the team until 2012.

Andersen signed with the [[Miami Heat]] in January 2013 and won a championship with them that same year. He and [[Oliver Lafayette]] are the only Blinn students to ever play in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ross|last=Coleman|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/580652-the-best-player-from-all-119-schools-represented-in-the-nba/page/9 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131222000008/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/580652-the-best-player-from-all-119-schools-represented-in-the-nba/page/9 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 22, 2013 |title=The Best Player From All 119 Schools Represented in the NBA|work=Bleacher Report|date=January 24, 2011|access-date=June 10, 2013}}</ref> He most recently played for the [[Dallas Power]] in the [[Big3]] league, helping them win the [[2018 Big3 season|2018 Big3 championship]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />
